correctness.rationale: The finite domain n in {2,4,6,8}, perfect-matching-generated face relation, edge labels and Klein-four maps are explicit. Independent tiling counts give 3,11,41,153 facets; exhaustive subface sets have 20,495,12375,309480 faces including empty. An algorithmic discrete-Morse pairing has respectively 0,1,1,2 nonempty augmented critical faces (dimensions 1,2,3,3) and the exact directed Hasse graph topologically sorts every face through 34,1679,62994,2101259 arrows; the unique empty-face pair is removed to give a single critical vertex. Thus the claimed finite sphere-wedge homotopy types follow. The exact signed fixed-face Lefschetz sums for all 16 group/width cases are computed from edge permutations and orientation signs; reduced homology concentration implies characters (1,-1,1,-1), (1,-1,-1,1), (2,0,0,2). Fourier inversion proves the n=8 trivial-plus-double-sign representation. Both standalone embedded verifiers were run with expected outputs. Only finite cases are claimed.

value.rationale: The result answers a motivated new equivariant question for the first wide three-row examples of a rectangular perfect-matching complex, not arbitrary numerical slices. It provides full finite homotopy types and, more importantly, exact geometric row/column reflection representations. At 3×8 the two rational degree-three homology classes split into inequivalent one-dimensional characters even though the nonequivariant space is S3 wedge S3; this is information neither existing homology ranks nor the general 2024 nonequivariant conjecture can predict. Four board widths form a natural progressive width-three benchmark; the 309480-face certificate is exhaustive and independent source code is included. The paper-sized all-width problem remains open.
